abhimana.gloss: opinion of oneself, self-conceit. In 18.12 it is offered to Śiva as a sacrificial dish.
abhimana.name: Abhimāna

advaya.gloss: non-duality: not “everything is one,” but that a second simply does not exist.
advaya.name: Advaya

amrta.gloss: nectar of immortality. In the hymns it flows from everywhere: from Śiva's body, from the name, from tears.
amrta.name: Amṛta

ananda.gloss: bliss — not pleasure, but the fullness of Consciousness content with itself.
ananda.name: Ānanda

anima.gloss: the power to shrink to an atom—the first of the eight superpowers. In the hymns it stands as an abbreviation for all of them: “aṇimā and so forth.”
anima.name: Aṇimā

anugraha.gloss: grace as one of the five acts of the Lord; its counterpart is nigraha, punishment.
anugraha.name: Anugraha

arcana.gloss: the same worship under another word; it stands more often where the action itself is meant.
arcana.name: Arcanā

asava.gloss: intoxicating drink. The word is chosen deliberately: for Utpaladeva devotion does not calm, it intoxicates.
asava.name: Āsava

asvada.gloss: tasting — the act itself: to taste, not to reason.
asvada.name: Āsvāda

atman.gloss: selfhood, one’s own nature. For Utpaladeva his own self and Śiva are one, and the whole book rests on the fact that this is not seen.
atman.name: Ātman

avesha.gloss: entering, being possessed: the state when that to which one is devoted enters into a person.
avesha.name: Āveśa

bhairava.gloss: the name of the Supreme Lord in Trika: the One who holds the universe, bears it, and draws it back in. Not a “terrifying deity,” but the fullness of Consciousness.
bhairava.name: Bhairava

bhakta.gloss: devotee — one who walks this path. In the hymns he laughs and weeps, and both come from the same source.
bhakta.name: Bhakta

bhakti.gloss: devotion — the main word of this book (94 times). For Utpaladeva it is not a feeling accompanying faith, but an independent path: higher than knowledge and yoga, and its fruit is itself.
bhakti.name: Bhakti

bhava.gloss: thing, being—and the state in which one abides. In Utpaladeva “bhāva” means now one, now the other, and often deliberately both at once.
bhava.name: Bhāva

bhavani.gloss: the Goddess as “wife of Bhava”; in Utpaladeva — the mother, while Śiva is the father (19.17).
bhavani.name: Bhavānī

bheda.gloss: difference, separateness — that by which the “great calamity” is upheld (7.1).
bheda.name: Bheda

camatkara.gloss: the thrill of recognition — a flash in which consciousness tastes itself.
camatkara.name: Camatkāra

cit.gloss: Consciousness as such, the pure capacity to shine. In the hymns everything is composed of it: cinmaya — “made of Consciousness.”
cit.name: Cit

citta.gloss: the consciousness of an individual person — that which can be defiled and which one asks to be purified.
citta.name: Citta

dasa.gloss: slave, servant. Utpaladeva constantly calls himself this — and for him it is not abasement but a title.
dasa.name: Dāsa

devi.gloss: Goddess — the Power of God, taken as His own inseparable aspect.
devi.name: Devī

dhyana.gloss: contemplation. In Utpaladeva it yields to touch: the festival of meeting is attained “by the rejection of the labour of contemplation” (17.4).
dhyana.name: Dhyāna

duhkha.gloss: grief, suffering. For the devotee, joined with steadfastness, it becomes bearable (10.16), or even tasty (16.11).
duhkha.name: Duḥkha

gauri.gloss: “the bright one” — the same name of the Goddess. Gaurī’s embrace in Utpaladeva is a measure of bliss (14.9).
gauri.name: Gaurī

guna.gloss: the three threads from which nature is woven: sattva, rajas, tamas. By themselves they are like lumps of earth and dance only when enlivened by the Lord (10.18).
guna.name: Guṇa

hara.gloss: “the remover” — Śiva as the One who takes away: both the world at the end of time, and the name, form, and movement of every thing (18.14).
hara.name: Hara

harsa.gloss: joy, exultation — that which makes the devotee's hairs stand on end.
harsa.name: Harṣa

ishvara.gloss: Lord: God taken from the side of power and freedom. In Utpaladeva — the One who, at the descent of Power, conducts no inquiry (13.11).
ishvara.name: Īśvara

japa.gloss: repetition of a mantra in a low voice. In 3.17 Śiva Himself shows by the beads that the whisperer and the Whispered-to are one.
japa.name: Japa

jnana.gloss: knowledge. For Utpaladeva it is not rejected, but placed below devotion: the highest stage of knowledge is devotion itself (9.9).
jnana.name: Jñāna

kriya.gloss: action. Together with knowledge — the two Powers of the Lord; in 20.16 Utpaladeva glorifies precisely the Power of action.
kriya.name: Kriyā

mada.gloss: intoxication, inebriation — the state produced by this drink.
mada.name: Mada

maheshvara.gloss: Great Lord. The word stands both as a name and as an indication that this power depends on nothing.
maheshvara.name: Maheśvara

mala.gloss: dirt, stain: that by which consciousness is closed off from itself.
mala.name: Mala

manas.gloss: the mind: that which runs about and which Utpaladeva reproaches for inconstancy.
manas.name: Manas

marga.gloss: road, path. In 20.12 Śaṅkara’s path is defined simply: there, where grief becomes joy.
marga.name: Mārga

maya.gloss: The power by which the Lord conceals Himself and manifests the world as separate. Not deception, but measure.
maya.name: Māyā

moksa.gloss: liberation. For ripe devotion it is merely a name (16.19), and by itself—“meagre” (19.14).
moksa.name: Mokṣa

mukti.gloss: the same liberation in another word; more often where the talk is of a state rather than an event.
mukti.name: Mukti

namas.gloss: “bow” — the word with which almost every stanza of the second hymn ends.
namas.name: Namas

natha.gloss: Lord, master, the one to whom one flees. In the vocative (nātha) — the most frequent address of the whole book.
natha.name: Nātha

nirvikalpa.gloss: without discursive thought — the state in which a thing is seen before it has been named.
nirvikalpa.name: Nirvikalpa

parameshvara.gloss: Supreme Lord — the same, but with emphasis on “there is nothing higher.”
parameshvara.name: Parameśvara

parvati.gloss: “daughter of the mountain” — the Goddess as daughter of Himavat.
parvati.name: Pārvatī

piyusa.gloss: and this too is nectar — the third word of the same series. Utpaladeva runs through them as one savors a taste.
piyusa.name: Pīyūṣa

prabhu.gloss: Lord — God as the ruler; in the vocative prabho.
prabhu.name: Prabhu

prakasha.gloss: Light — the side of Reality by which it manifests. Brighter than a thousand suns, and therefore invisible (3.19).
prakasha.name: Prakāśa

prasada.gloss: grace, favour—and also “clarification”: that by which the murky becomes transparent.
prasada.name: Prasāda

pratibha.gloss: illumination — knowledge that comes by itself, without learning or inference.
pratibha.name: Pratibhā

puja.gloss: worship, service to the deity. The seventeenth hymn is entirely about it: for the devotee it proceeds both in sleep and in delusion.
puja.name: Pūjā

raga.gloss: passion, attraction — and at the same time “color.” Utpaladeva uses both senses: his love for Śiva is also rāga.
raga.name: Rāga

rasa.gloss: juice, taste: that by which a thing is taken onto the tongue. For Utpaladeva devotion is precisely tasted, not performed.
rasa.name: Rasa

samsara.gloss: the cycle of births — and at the same time all of ordinary life. For the devotee it becomes a “pond for play” (3.15).
samsara.name: Saṁsāra

samvid.gloss: Consciousness — not “my consciousness,” but that single principle by which anything at all exists.
samvid.name: Saṁvid

shakti.gloss: the Power of God, His I-Consciousness: the same Reality taken as will and movement.
shakti.name: Śakti

shaktipata.gloss: descent of Power: the grace by which the Lord reveals Himself. In 13.11 Utpaladeva asks why no inquiry occurs under it—and this stanza is quoted in full by the Tantrāloka 13.290.
shaktipata.name: Śaktipāta

shambhu.gloss: “source of good” — another name of Śiva, the most frequent in the vocative case: śambho, “O Śambhu.”
shambhu.name: Śambhu

shankara.gloss: “creating good” — a name of Śiva that Utpaladeva calls a medicine: this very word on the tongue enters even the hearts of animals (4.13).
shankara.name: Śaṅkara

sharana.gloss: refuge, protection. “I have come under Your protection”—the last line of the second hymn.
sharana.name: Śaraṇa

shiva.gloss: God as the resting side of Reality — the Light of Consciousness, not different from His own Power. In the hymns, not an abstract principle, but the One addressed as “you.”
shiva.name: Śiva

shrikantha.gloss: “fair-throated” — Śiva, whose throat turns blue from the poison kālakūṭa, drunk for the sake of saving the worlds.
shrikantha.name: Śrīkaṇṭha

siddhi.gloss: perfection, superpower—and at the same time “success, what has come true.” Both senses work at once in Utpaladeva.
siddhi.name: Siddhi

stuti.gloss: praise, hymn. The very word stotra in the title of the book is from the same root.
stuti.name: Stuti

sudha.gloss: the same nectar under another word; most often — "nectar of devotion."
sudha.name: Sudhā

svamin.gloss: Lord, master of the house. The word is domestic, and Utpaladeva chooses it where he speaks of himself as a slave and a member of the household.
svamin.name: Svāmin

svatantrya.gloss: Absolute Freedom — that which makes the Lord the Lord. According to the introduction to the book, to attain It is to be liberated.
svatantrya.name: Svātantrya

tattva.gloss: principle, level of Reality; there are thirty-six of them — from Śiva down to earth. In 17.11 they are what one worships with.
tattva.name: Tattva

tryambaka.gloss: “three-eyed” — Śiva with a third eye on his forehead. Utpaladeva calls this eye the sole mark of otherworldly majesty (10.6).
tryambaka.name: Tryambaka

uma.gloss: name of the Goddess, consort of Śiva; Utpaladeva calls Him umeśa — “Lord of Umā.”
uma.name: Umā

unmada.gloss: madness, frenzy: intoxication carried to the point where a man dances and cries out amid the world.
unmada.name: Unmāda

upacara.gloss: ritual service: offering water, a flower, a lamp. In the devotee, says Utpaladeva, these services are replaced by taste (17.40).
upacara.name: Upacāra

upaya.gloss: means, path to the goal. The hymns stand apart: devotion here is not a means but the goal itself.
upaya.name: Upāya

utsava.gloss: festival. For Utpaladeva worship is not a rite but precisely a festival, and this word recurs some twenty times.
utsava.name: Utsava

vapus.gloss: body, form. Śiva’s body in the hymns is not an image for contemplation but that which is touched.
vapus.name: Vapus

vasana.gloss: trace left by past deeds — and at the same time “fragrance.” The whole of stanza 5.19 rests on this double meaning.
vasana.name: Vāsanā

vibhu.gloss: All-pervading: the One for whom there is nowhere to extend, because He is already everywhere.
vibhu.name: Vibhu

vikalpa.gloss: discursive thought: that which cuts the one into “this” and “not this.”
vikalpa.name: Vikalpa

vimarsha.gloss: the echo, the self-awareness of Light: “this — I am.” Without it, Light would shine without knowing of itself.
vimarsha.name: Vimarśa

vishva.gloss: the universe as a whole; for Utpaladeva it is now fuel for fire, now the offering, now the fire itself (2.2).
vishva.name: Viśva

yoga.gloss: union and the way to attain it. Utpaladeva calls it a deception—the thought that the Lord can be obtained by yoga “sometimes and somewhere” (1.16).
yoga.name: Yoga
